summary: Standards, Spec, and Security completed change-sensitive review over the target merge-base through the full working tree.
Review found two blocking Spec contradictions, including one shared Standards correctness blocker, plus four non-blocking medium findings.
rationale: Stopped before remediation because a blocking Spec finding requires user guidance on whether the approved specification or implementation is wrong.

verification.reason: Review was read-only and evaluated the completed Test evidence, including the passing 43-test Vitest and 32-test Playwright full suite.

findings.evidence: Production section records contain only section titles, while ability records omit visible labels and containing character names. Queries for authoritative body prose such as unsafe movement return no result; synthetic search fixtures are richer than production records.
findings.violated: Correctness and test-quality properties requiring complete full-text search over authoritative rendered rules and trustworthy production-representative evidence.
findings.issue: Search misses ordinary visible rules prose and current passing tests conceal the incomplete production index.
findings.remediation: Index each complete authoritative section source span, retain narrower ranked records, and add production-artifact plus browser ordering coverage.

findings.evidence: Canonical restoration rejects snapshots whose rulesVersion differs from the bundled RULES_VERSION, removes the Match from UI state, and then Rules opens the current bundled version. The direct resolver test does not exercise persistence restoration.
findings.violated: Solution decisions and acceptance criteria 3 and 4 requiring active Match saved-version binding and a clear exact-version unavailable error without fallback.
findings.issue: The required unavailable-version surface is unreachable for a persisted older Match and the UI substitutes the bundled version after rejecting that Match.
findings.remediation: Restore internally consistent Matches with their saved rulesVersion, then let the Rules surface report unavailable exact content; add a browser workflow proving state and events remain unchanged.

findings.evidence: Universal section search records contain only titles. A query such as referee judgment returns no production result despite that phrase appearing in the authoritative rules; browser evidence covers only an ability name.
findings.violated: Full-text search solution, implementation decisions for universal section records, and user stories 17 through 24.
findings.issue: Search cannot return most universal rules prose and the production ranking behavior is unproven.
findings.remediation: Populate section records from authoritative body text or anchored contained rules, with production-artifact phrase and ranking tests.

findings.evidence: Punctuation becomes token separators, so Nature’s Renewal and the punctuation-free query Natures Renewal normalize differently and do not match.
findings.violated: Acceptance criterion 15 and user story 17 requiring punctuation-insensitive search.
findings.issue: Omitting punctuation breaks matching for authoritative apostrophe-bearing names.
findings.remediation: Canonicalize punctuation so punctuated and unpunctuated forms compare equivalently and add regression tests.

findings.evidence: Nested reference objects remain mutable, and JSON serialization removes build-time array freezes while the emitted module freezes only the root.
findings.violated: The requirement for one immutable versioned reference artifact shared by rendering and search.
findings.issue: Consumers can mutate nested reference or search data and make rendering diverge from search.
findings.remediation: Deep-freeze emitted nested arrays and objects and add nested immutability contract checks.

findings.evidence: Prefix-related terms such as back and backstab produce overlapping ranges; rendering skips the later overlapping range and only visibly marks Back.
findings.violated: Acceptance criterion 20 and user story 23 requiring every matched term to be highlighted.
findings.issue: All terms match but overlapping terms are not all represented by the rendered highlight.
findings.remediation: Merge overlapping ranges into a visible union or otherwise render equivalent coverage, with API and browser regression tests.

findings.evidence: Only generated reference HTML is sanitized. Structured headings, roster values, and card fields can retain raw HTML and are later inserted into innerHTML; event-handler payloads in section titles or character names pass generation and reach browser sinks.
findings.violated: Repository-authored rules content must not become executable browser markup through structured Markdown fields.
findings.issue: A malicious or compromised rules-only change can execute script in the application origin and alter displayed controls or local Match data.
findings.remediation: Reject raw HTML or normalize all structured fields to text, escape every value and attribute before innerHTML insertion or construct nodes with textContent, and add injection contract/browser tests.

blockers: User must choose whether the saved-Match rulesVersion requirement or the current restoration behavior is authoritative.
User must choose whether full-text search remains required; if it does, authorize remediation of the production index and evidence before review reruns.

rationale: Kept the approved version-binding and full-text-search specification by generalizing persistence consistency around the saved version rather than substituting bundled rules.
Retained narrow character, ability, and quick-reference records beside complete section records so exact cards rank first while full authoritative prose remains searchable.
Rejected repository-authored raw HTML at the build boundary and escaped structured browser values as defense in depth because the generated artifact crosses a browser execution boundary.

summary: Standards and Spec confirmed every high and critical blocker resolved; Security completed the full affected follow-up with no findings.
Recorded one new non-blocking excerpt-length issue on both Standards and Spec axes.
rationale: Accepted the follow-up because review policy blocks only high and critical findings and all previously blocking behavior now matches the approved specification.

Recorded the shared excerpt defect separately on Standards and Spec because it violates both a correctness property and the short-excerpt acceptance requirement; policy forbids another automatic loop for medium findings.

verification.reason: Follow-up review was read-only and relied on the remediation evidence: 40 targeted Vitest checks, 14 phone/tablet Playwright workflows, and passing TypeScript, build, lint, and format checks.

findings.evidence: matchingRanges collects every occurrence and excerptFor spans from the first to last. In production section 15, query duration produces an 11,208-character excerpt from an 11,693-character section.
findings.violated: Correctness property requiring each result to show a short matching excerpt while full-section indexing remains usable.
findings.issue: Repeated common terms can render almost an entire section inside one search result.
findings.remediation: Choose a bounded matching window containing representative occurrences for every distinct term and add a production-record length regression.

findings.evidence: Production queries can create 647-character, 1,192-character, or 10,703-character excerpts because excerptFor has no enforced maximum when matches are far apart.
findings.violated: Acceptance criterion 20 and user story 23 requiring a short scannable matching excerpt.
findings.issue: Common multi-occurrence queries can render most of a large rules section before the referee selects the source.
findings.remediation: Cap excerpts using the smallest useful cluster or bounded window that preserves at least one highlight per term, with production unit and browser evidence.
